subject: math
title: Equivalent Fractions
seo_title: Grade 4 Equivalent Fractions Worksheets: Fraction Models, Missing Numbers, Number Lines and Hundredths
standard_text: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 equivalent fractions worksheets with pictures: see equal amounts in fraction bars and area models, find the missing number, simplify, use number lines, and change tenths to hundredths. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number. The amount stays the same.
key_sub: 2/3 = 4/6: each third is cut into 2 equal parts, so there are twice as many parts, each half as big. Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not work.
body_html:
What equivalent fractions are

Equivalent fractions name the same amount with different numbers. Cut every part into the same number of smaller parts: you get more parts, each smaller, but the shaded amount does not change.

The rule: multiply or divide both numbers by the same number

Do thisExampleWhy it works
Multiply the top and bottom by the same number23 = 812 (× 4)Each part is cut into 4 smaller parts
Divide the top and bottom by the same number68 = 34 (÷ 2)Every 2 small parts are joined into 1 bigger part
Example

Find the missing number: 35 = ?10

5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the bottom by 2. Do the same to the top: 3 × 2 = 6.

Answer: 6

On a number line

Equivalent fractions are at the same point on a number line.

Tenths and hundredths

Example

Write 14 in hundredths.

4 × 25 = 100, so multiply the top by 25 too: 1 × 25 = 25.

Answer: 25100

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the same number: 23 → 45Multiply the top and bottom: 23 = 46
Multiplying only the bottom: 12 → 14Change both numbers by the same number
Thinking 48 is more than 12 because it has more partsMore parts means smaller parts. The amount is the same
Writing 310 as 3100Multiply both by 10: 30100

faq.q: How do you explain equivalent fractions to a 4th grader?
faq.a: Show the same bar shaded two ways. Cut each third of 2/3 in half: there are twice as many parts, each half as big, so 2/3 = 4/6. The amount does not change.

faq.q: How do you find an equivalent fraction?
faq.a: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number. For 2/3 = ?/12, 3 × 4 = 12, so 2 × 4 = 8 and 2/3 = 8/12.

faq.q: Why can’t you add the same number to the top and bottom?
faq.a: Adding changes the amount. 1/2 + 1 on top and bottom gives 2/3, which is more than 1/2. Only multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number keeps the amount the same.

faq.q: How do you change tenths to hundredths?
faq.a: Multiply the top and bottom by 10. 3/10 = 30/100, because each tenth is 10 hundredths.
